task.description:
WF-02, step 5 — write the tests of REQ-104 by the design docs/design/REQ-104-e2e-chrome-kit.md (sections 10 "criterion → test", 11 "The tests", 12 "Replacement table", 16 "Mutants") and the section "Step 5" of docs/workflows/WF-02-development.md. The code passed gates 3 and 4 (third pass PASS: handoffs/E2E104-20261103-01/step-04f-security-reviewer.json and step-04g-reviewer.json). Read the design completely, the block REQ-104 in docs/requirements.yaml, docs/quality-bar.md, docs/anti-patterns.md.

YOUR FILES (design section 3): tools/test/e2e/smoke.e2e.js (SMK-01..SMK-13, real Chrome), tools/test/e2e-kit.test.js (E2K-01..E2K-61, 40 tests), tools/test/fixtures/e2e/specs/*.e2e.js and tools/test/fixtures/e2e/tap/*.txt (plain fixtures, TAP texts normalized so they hold NO absolute path — design 11.3), and the replacement of the six guard tests HC-02, HC-03, HO-54, PK-7b, LP-3, CTL-13 by section 12 (fix them FIRST, without weakening: the number of `test(` and `assert.` in the old files is not lower than at the tag base/E2E104-20261103-01). You do not change code of the kit; if a test needs a code change, write it in result.issues (the edit is CODE-FIXER's and the gates 3 and 4 run again).

MUST ALSO COVER (read these handoffs' result.issues yourself and take every item): step-02-backend-dev.json (I1..I5: the stand-in modes, the contract details, criterion 4 needs smoke.e2e.js to exist), step-04b-code-fixer.json (I2: R-F1 full CHROME_NOT_FOUND text, R-F2 stand-in mode `no-upgrade` and CALL_TIMEOUT, R-F5 WAIT_TIMEOUT last-protocol-error text, R-F6 START_EXITED well under 1 s, R-F7 SCREENSHOT_FAILED, S-F1 stopped runner with hung/blocked spec leaves no process and no folder + registry validation, S-F2 safeText table and the 20-entry cap, S-F3 `--no-proxy-server` in the E2K-25 argument list, S-F4 PATH_REFUSED for NUL / long name / link loop), step-04e-code-fixer.json (F1 a Chrome launched with an `env` option that lacks the registry variable still gets a record; F2 newline or leading `::` in argv or SAI_CHROME never starts a log line and a 100 KB argument is cut; F3 `signalGroup` returns false for 0, 1, negative, fractional, NaN, string and true for a live group; a record with pgid 0 or 1 is ignored), step-04d/04g (reviewer notes for TEST-DESIGNER), and the Low remarks N1-N6 of the design gate step-01f-code-design-validator.json (N3: a two-hook case if "at once" stays; N5: pin or not the exact line and column; N6: build outside paths at run time). Tests for hung stand-in modes must not hang the run (AP-116); for `exit-early` use a start limit well above 1 s (one early START_TIMEOUT at 1 s was seen). Oracles are your own: do not import rules from the kit's source for the expected values, except the kit's public API under test.

BAR: Q5 a test per criterion (1-13), failure tests check the state did not change, tests independent of each other and of the clock, no skip/todo/`|| true`/eslint-disable, no secret, no absolute machine path in any committed file (npm run traces), the forbidden words only built from parts (design 11.1/11.3). New logic needs mutants: apply at least 20 of the 72 mutants of design section 16 (the design names the test that catches each) in a TEMPORARY COPY outside the project, record in self_check: what is broken → which tests failed → how many; the working tree must not change (list of hashes before and after) and the tests are green again after. The step is handed in with a passing check: after your work `cd tools && npm test` must be green (only a failure proven not to be caused by this work is allowed) and `cd tools && npm run e2e` must run the real Chrome smoke spec and exit 0 on this Mac with `e2e: browser=` printed; run `npm run check` once at the end if the time allows (about 5 minutes).
SAFETY ON THIS MAC: one agent at a time; at most three full `npm test` runs in the whole step, mutant runs only of the relevant test files; Chrome only through the kit's own cleanup; kill any Chrome you start by process id; remove only temp folders you made; never rm inside the project (a test that creates a temp folder removes it itself); format new files with `cd tools && npx prettier --write <your files>`; `npm run lint`. Do not commit. No name of another project in any file.

npm test green and npm run e2e green with the real Chrome

Design vs build: (a) design 11.3 lists the fixture contents; sleep-chrome.e2e.js also reads SAI_FIXTURE_BLOCK (1 = block the event loop with Atomics.wait instead of waiting; used by E2K-45) and leaves the mark <pidfile>.term in a SIGTERM handler (used by E2K-38 to tell an orderly stop from a kill, needed because the registry of browsers now hides the difference for M59); its pid key is `spec`, not `file`, because E2K-34 forbids the text `file:` in fixtures. (b) The design says hang-ignore-term is used by E2K-17; as the backend developer wrote (step-02 I4d) no Browser can be built on it, so E2K-17 uses ok-ignore-term and E2K-11 uses hang-ignore-term for the START_TIMEOUT kill. (c) SMK-13 has no proxy trial: Chrome on macOS takes proxies from the system, not from the environment, so a positive control cannot be made; the flag --no-proxy-server is pinned by the exact argument list of E2K-25 and mutant X01. (d) Design E2K-50 section 10 text mentions a rule `://` that 11.1 does not have (N1 of the design gate): the test follows 11.1. (e) SMK-09, SMK-10, SMK-11, SMK-12 sit under criteria 3 and 5 (N2).

For ORCH / DOC-UPDATER: X13 is an equivalent mutant. The sweep of the registry after each spec (runner.js, 'a browser the spec did not close ... is killed now') changes nothing a test can see, because a failed or stopped spec ends the run and the finally of runAll sweeps again; it would matter only for a spec that passes and leaves a browser running while the next spec starts. If that case is wanted it needs a spec fixture that leaves a live browser and exits with code 0 (the kit's own exit handler normally prevents it). Not built: no criterion asks for it.

Not tested, as ordered by the earlier gates: the START_FAILED messages in browser.js (two places) still print the SAI_CHROME path raw (SECURITY-REVIEWER I1, CODE-FIXER 04e I2, Low, accepted); when someone fixes them a test is to be added next to E2K-42 (the lookup messages of findChrome are already covered there). The wait of 100 ms after a load (LOAD_SETTLE_MS, step-02 I3) is exercised only through SMK-08; no unit test pins the number. The mutants M63 (hook added late) and M30 (a module flag makes a second start fail) were not built: M63 has no one-place form here, M30 needs a flag the code does not have; their effects are covered by E2K-38 (the preflight case) and by 'a second start works' in E2K-10...E2K-14.

Time-based assertions use wide limits (stop within 8 to 9 s, start failures within 5 s) and lower bounds only where the code must wait (E2K-15 >= 450 ms, E2K-17 >= 450 ms, E2K-39 b >= 900 ms). The full suite ran green twice in a row under the parallel load of npm test (2184 of 2184); if a slow machine makes one of them flaky, the longest are E2K-33 (7 s), E2K-43 and E2K-45 (about 5.5 s each), E2K-39 (2.5 s), all with the 30000 ms limit. Every test makes its own folders under a private temporary root and the last test (E2K-51) asserts that the root is empty, so a leaked folder turns that test red.

Candidates for docs/anti-patterns.md (Q13): (1) a mutation harness that kills a timed-out test process leaves the browsers that process started, because they sit in their own process group: kill them by the private temporary folder in their command line; (2) a mutant that makes the kit ignore the stand-in starts the real Chrome in every test, about 4 minutes per such mutant (M02); (3) files written to the scratch folder came back reformatted and with an escape \u2028 turned into the real character, which broke a regular expression (fixed by writing the check as a loop over character codes).
